A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AnyTouch framework and TacQuad dataset. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete Appendix A.1–A.13 are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original static-perception evaluations, sensor-transfer analyses, real-world pouring experiments, and appendix ablation and cross-sensor generation results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results in Section 5 and Appendices A.9–A.10, including Tables 1–4, 6, and 7.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same unified image/video inputs, masked modeling, multimodal alignment, cross-sensor matching, universal sensor tokens, and two-stage training. Figure 4's corrected method name does not indicate a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same nine training datasets, four downstream evaluation datasets, pouring task, and cross-sensor generation tasks. TacQuad's sensor coverage and coarse- and fine-grained subsets are unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1–4 and 7, including CLIP, VIT-LENS-2, TLV-Link, OmniBind, UniTouch, and T3 in their respective comparisons. Newly cited Higuera and Gupta works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The data splits, training budgets, linear-probing evaluations, pouring fine-tuning/freezing conditions, and generation metrics remain unchanged. The corresponding protocols in Section 5 and Appendices A.3, A.6, A.8, and A.10 match.

E4.justification: Both retain the sensor-transfer analysis, t-SNE component analysis, modality/component ablations in Table 6, and annotation examples. Figure 4's relabeling introduces no new analysis or finding.

E5.justification: Both report ten real-world pouring test runs summarized by mean error. There are no changes to run-count disclosures, seed information, uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance testing.

E6.justification: Reported result entries, values, and findings are unchanged across the main text and appendices. For example, fine-tuned AnyTouch pouring error remains 1.56 g in Table 4, and GelSight Mini-to-DuraGel generation MSE remains 0.2159 in Table 7.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and loss expressions in Section 4 and Appendix A.2 are unchanged. Equation 6 gains terminal punctuation only; no mathematical correction, theorem, or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: TacQuad, unified static-dynamic multisensor representation learning, and improved perception and cross-sensor transfer. Their scientific scope and claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations of sensor transfer and component effects remain unchanged. Appendices A.11–A.13 retain the same frame-count tradeoffs, discussion of other sensor types, and limitations concerning dataset scale, sensor diversity, and evaluation on a single dynamic manipulation task.

D1.justification: Data filtering, annotation prompts, architecture and optimizer details, training schedules, hardware, and robotic setup are unchanged. Both PDFs provide the same code, dataset, and model availability statement and project link.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Higuera et al. (2024), Sparsh, and Gupta et al. (2025), Sensor-invariant tactile representation, with corresponding references. A Girdhar et al. (2023) citation is removed from the audio example but remains elsewhere. This modestly expands coverage without substantially changing positioning.

P1.justification: There are limited wording edits in related work, an added period after Equation 6, and terminology correction in Figure 4. The narrative, section order, and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 4's three 'UltraTouch' panel headings become 'AnyTouch', while the plotted relationships, legend, and caption are retained. Added references cause minor bibliography reflow; no figures or tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves related-work coverage by acknowledging Sparsh and Sensor-invariant tactile representation, and resolves Figure 4's inconsistent method naming. These improve scholarly context and clarity, while the methods, empirical evidence, and limitations remain unchanged.
